stories.title: PK Mishra applauds PM Modi’s 'visionary approach' during Gujarat earthquake and Covid-19 crisis
stories.summary: Speaking to reporters after addressing the inaugural day of NITI Aayog National Workshop, Mishra said that he has witnessed the then-Gujarat CM's leadership in the aftermath of the earthquake in 2001.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Speaking to reporters after addressing the inaugural day of NITI Aayog National Workshop, Mishra said that he has witnessed the then-Gujarat CM's leadership in the aftermath of the earthquake in 2001.

New Delhi: PK Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, on Tuesday, credited PM Narendra Modi's "visionary and determined" approach in "leading Gujarat out of the earthquake tragedy in 2001, during the latter's tenure as the Chief Minister, and similar leadership response during the uncertainty of the Covid-19 pandemic".
"I remember when Narendra Modi became Chief Minister for the first time, nine months after the Bhuj earthquake in Gujarat.
It was one of the biggest challenges he faced once he became the Chief Minister.
It was a very devastating earthquake: 14,000 people died, and a million houses were damaged or destroyed.
How to effectively bring about rehabilitation and reconstruction in order to meet that challenge, that, in fact, showed us his leadership qualities," he added.

According to Mishra, PM Modi doesn't believe in just announcing a scheme and giving instructions to officers, rather he likes to ensure that all the benefits reach the last mile and himself monitors it regularly.

Recalling an instance, the Principal Secretary said: "PM Modi had asked the officers who had written the rehabilitation policy of a village to visit the affected region during weekend and report to him in the weekly Monday meeting."
"After their visit, the officials said that some aspects of their policy were not appropriate and themselves suggested changes.
It is just an example of how he (Prime Minister) ensures that the changes are effective," he added.
Mishra said that several bold initiatives were taken during the Covid-19 pandemic, under PM Modi's leadership.
"During that time, nobody knew what effects the pandemic will have, even in other countries.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Applies Doctrine Of Indoor Management, Says Company's Boardroom Dispute Cannot Invalidate Sale To Bona Fide Third-Party
stories.title: Supreme Court Applies Doctrine Of Indoor Management, Says Company's Boardroom Dispute Cannot Invalidate Sale To Bona Fide Third-Party
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has observed that a third-party purchaser of a company's asset relying on a Company's Board Resolution meeting to undertake the purchase is protected under the Transfer of Property Act, and the sale cannot be invalidated merely because there's an internal dispute regarding the authority to execute the sale deed.

According to the Court, the unrelated third party cannot be expected to verify the internal affairs of the company, particularly whether the Board meeting authorising the transaction was validly convened.

A bench of Justice Sanjay Kumar and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva set aside the concurrent findings of NCLAT and NCLT, which had ruled against the unrelated third party, i.e., the Appellant-M/s Elaine Info Solutions Pvt.

Ltd., on the pretext that the Appellant was not able to establish that another Director of the Respondent company participated in the board meeting, in which the resolution to sell the company's asset was passed.

Noting that the Appellant is an unrelated third party to the Respondent's internal affairs and cannot be expected to know about the company's meeting and passing of the resolution, hence, a sale deed executed pursuant to the Respondent's board resolution cannot be cancelled merely because the Appellant failed to prove the participation of another director in the meeting.
“The Doctrine of Indoor Management would clearly come to apply in the present case.
Both NCLT and NCLAT have primarily acted by holding that the resolution of the Board of Directors had not been passed and the sale deed executed based thereon was invalid.
Appellant, being an unrelated third-party would have no knowledge of the indoor affairs of the Company… It may be noted that the Appellant is a third-party to the affairs of the Company.
The Board Resolution dated 01.08.2015 is alleged to have been passed in a meeting held on the same date 01.08.2015.

Though the sale deed dated 04.09.2015 refers to a resolution of the Board Meeting dated 01.08.2015, Appellant cannot be attributed to have any knowledge of the same as the holding of the meeting and passing of the said resolution would be within the personal knowledge of the Directors/shareholders of the Company.”, the Court observed.
The case arose from a dispute within Respondent company-M/s J & A Avenues India Private Limited, whose shares were equally held by a mother and her son, both of whom were also directors.

The mother had approached the NCLT under Section 241 of the Companies Act, 2013, alleging that her son had transferred 9 acres and 28 guntas of the company's land to the Appellant, Elaine Info Solutions Pvt.

The Supreme Court on Tuesday (November 17) reserved its order on a public interest litigation filed by financial journalist Sucheta Dalal seeking a centralised, searchable database to help legal heirs trace unclaimed financial assets of deceased persons.

The public can access the disclosures made by companies through the portal of the IEPF authority.

The ASG said that these measures fulfil the prayers sought in the petition.
Regarding the steps taken by the Department of Financial Services, the ASG said that Section 26 of the Banking Regulation Act deals with unclaimed deposits.
Further, policy measures have been adopted to ease the processing of claims.
After the 2025 Banking Laws Amendment Act, up to four persons can be nominated.

In a significant development in the fake birth certificate case involving Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan and his family, the Supreme Court on Tuesday dismissed an appeal filed by the Uttar Pradesh government challenging the relief granted to the politician.
The court also extended relief to Khan's wife, Tazeen Fatima, and son, Abdullah Azam Khan, by staying their convictions.
A bench comprising Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu dismissed the state's challenge and granted Fatima and Abdullah relief similar to the one previously extended to Khan.
The case dates back to allegations that Abdullah had obtained two birth certificates carrying different dates of birth.
While one certificate recorded his date of birth as January 1, 1993, the other mentioned September 30, 1990.
On October 18, 2023, a Rampur MP-MLA court convicted Azam Khan, Fatima and Abdullah in the case and sentenced all three to seven years in prison.
The family subsequently approached the Allahabad High Court seeking relief against the conviction.
In May 2024, the High Court stayed Khan's conviction and sentence but declined to grant similar relief to his wife and son.
The Uttar Pradesh government then moved the Supreme Court, challenging the relief granted to Khan.
The state's appeal has now been dismissed, while Fatima and Abdullah have also secured a stay on their convictions.
However, the Supreme Court's order does not amount to an acquittal.

stories.summary: Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh), Nov 17 : A massive gas leak occurred from an ONGC gas drilling well in Andhra Pradesh’s Dr B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district on Tuesday, triggering panic among people in surrounding villages. The gas leak from the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) rig occurred near Geddada village in Mamidikuduru mandal. According to officials, the gas began leaking around 4:30 a.m. on Tuesday, accompanied by a loud noise, and is currently spewing out in large volumes. The incident triggered panic among residents and commuters on the National Highway 216. Gas was reportedly spreading to nearby villages, with residents complaining of a strong gas smell. People living in the vicinity and motorists passing through the highway ran to safety after noticing the gas leak. Police halted vehicular movement on the Geddada-Mamidikuduru highway as a precautionary measure. ONGC officials and police were alerted, while specialised teams were being mobilised to contain the leak. A control team from Narsapur left for the spot to contain the blowout. The officials stated that there have been no fires so far and that the wellhead remains secure. ONGC personnel were taking measures to prevent the gas from spreading near the ground level. Fire-fighters arranged the water umbrella around the rig to prevent fire. Meanwhile, Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu has spoken with officials regarding a gas leak incident. He directed that residents in the affected areas be evacuated to safer locations. The Chief Minister said public safety must be given the highest priority. He said ONGC must take immediate action, deploying specialised technical teams to bring the gas leak under control. Noting that such incidents have occurred frequently of late, the Chief Minister instructed officials to immediately engage with ONGC management. He has ordered a review of safety protocols in consultation with the ONGC Chairman and other senior officials of the organisation. Authorities have already evacuated residents living within a one-kilometre radius of the gas well. As a precautionary safety measure, diesel generators and other equipment have been shut down and removed from the vicinity. A cementing team is arriving at the site to completely plug the gas well leak. ONGC officials have stated that the gas leak incident will be brought fully under control within the next 4-5 hours. On Monday, the Finance Minister held the second pre-Budget consultation with experts and stakeholders from the agriculture and rural development sectors. The discussions focused on measures to strengthen rural growth, boost farm incomes and enhance the contribution of agriculture to the broader economy. The meeting was attended by senior officials from the Department of Economic Affairs, the Department of Fisheries and the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. Earlier on the same day, the finance minister chaired the first round of consultations with leading economists, seeking views on macroeconomic trends, growth prospects and policy priorities for the upcoming fiscal year. In addition, the government has also been engaging with industry bodies as part of the consultation process. In recent interactions with the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PHDCCI), industry representatives called for customs duty rationalisation on key industrial raw materials and energy inputs to improve India's competitiveness as a manufacturing hub. stories.title: Two Indian finalists in Prince William’s ‘Earthshot Prize’ race
stories.summary: For over three decades, Mahila Housing Trust (MHT) has been working to improve living conditions in low-income urban communities through programmes to facilitate access to water, sanitation, community infrastructure and public spaces etc. But it was in the mid-2010s that the Ahmedabad-based non-profit began to recognise another increasingly urgent challenge: The impact that climate change had on the homes and the livelihoods of the poor.As temperatures soared globally, Gujarat, a state accustomed to hot, dry summers, began to experience severe effects. Homes with tin-sheet roofs heated up rapidly, while those with concrete roofs and inadequate ventilation trapped even more heat. “And productivity was affected, whether you were working from those homes or, like a construction worker, going out to work in the heat,” says Bijal Brahmbhatt, executive director, MHT.In 2015, MHT introduced cool roofs, coated with a specialised reflective layer to reduce indoor temperatures by two to five degrees Celsius. The women we knew had an innate habit of saving, but those could be withdrawn. We wanted an instrument that they could not dip into, but that would give them a payout in an emergency,” adds Brahmbhatt. Launched in 2023, the product uses 40 years of weather data to establish temperature thresholds that, when breached, triggers a payout for policyholders—it has insured 49,000 women so far, and will now be taken beyond borders to Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and the Philippines. With the EVs, while they are not the most profitable right now—in fact, not at all—we will be able to make profits if we are able to deliver the volumes,” says Mishra.The choice of India as a host itself is curious given the country’s dual reality. We've had more finalists and winners from here than any other country.” Over its six editions, India has produced seven finalists and four winners.“Often, the world’s emerging economies are presented with false choices: Growth or the environment. Wherever we go around the world, we want the work we're doing to be informed by people who are on the ground and have decades of experience,” says Knauf. The organisation has hired an India director, Smita Rakesh, a veteran in the impact investing space, to continue the work and connect the network to the climate and nature innovation ecosystem in India.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu government cannot ban transportation of minerals to other States, rules Madras High Court
stories.summary: Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan declare as unconstitutional Rule 3A of the Tamil Nadu Prevention of Illegal Mining, Tansportation and Storage of Minerals and Mineral Dealers Rules, 2011
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'chief justice' in summary weight 25.2
article_sentences: The Madras High Court on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) declared as unconstitutional Rule 3A of the Tamil Nadu Prevention of Illegal Mining, Transportation and Storage of Minerals and Mineral Dealers Rules, 2011 which empowers the Director of Geology and Mining to impose a temporary ban on transportation of minerals to other States.

First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan held that the rule, inserted by way of an amendment on July 9, 2026, was unconstitutional and also ultravires the provisions of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulations) Act, 1957, a central legislation under which the rules had been framed.

Consequentially, the judges also quashed an order passed by the Director of Geology and Mining on July 27, 2026 imposing a temporary ban on transportation of rough stones and their aggregates to other States, except to Puducherry and the Karaikal region for a period of three months, that was later extended by another three months from October 27, in order to ensure adequate availability in Tamil Nadu.

The orders were passed on a batch of writ petitions filed both in the principal seat of the High Court in Chennai as well as its Madurai Bench challenging the constitutional validity of Rule 3A introduced through an amendment to the statutory rules on July 9, 2026 as well as the consequential temporary ban order passed by the Director of Geology and Mining.

However, a host of crusher and quarry owners associations as well as individual owners of such facilities had approached the High Court contending that the newly-introduced statutory rule was ultravires Articles 301 (Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse throughout the territory of India) and 304(b) (power of a State legislature to impose reasonable restrictions on the freedom of trade, commerce or intercourse in public interest).

The petitioners had also contended that the statutory rule was ultravires Section 23(C)(1) of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957, a central legislation which empowers the State governments to frame rules for preventing illegal mining, transportation and storage of minerals.

stories.headline: India's CAD may touch 1.2% of GDP in FY27
stories.title: India's CAD may touch 1.2% of GDP in FY27

article_sentences: New Delhi: India's current account deficit (CAD) could remain close to 1.2 per cent of GDP in FY27, but sustained high crude oil prices and seasonal gold demand could put pressure on the country's external balance, according to a report by Union Bank of India.

The bank said the outlook for India's current account and overall balance of payments remained uncertain, with oil prices, services exports and gold imports likely to determine the extent of external sector pressure in the coming months.
"Though upside risks to CAD come from further gold buying during festive season; relief in crude prices in the H2 FY 27 could somewhat ease-out import pressures," the report said.

The caution comes after India's merchandise trade deficit widened to a 12-month high of USD 39.88 billion in October, from USD 30.21 billion in September, as imports rose to a record USD 89.35 billion.
Exports increased to USD 49.47 billion during the month.
The services trade surplus remained nearly flat at USD 19.8 billion, taking the overall trade deficit to USD 20.09 billion from USD 11 billion in September.
Gold, non-oil non-gold and oil imports contributed to the widening merchandise deficit.
Gold import volumes rose to an estimated 69.4 metric tonnes in October from 23.4 metric tonnes in September, while the non-oil, non-gold deficit reached a record USD 19.9 billion.
Union Bank's CAD projection assumes crude oil prices in the range of USD 95-100 per barrel.
It estimated that every USD 10 per barrel movement in oil prices could affect India's annual current account balance by nearly USD 15 billion.

The report also flagged risks from volatile non-oil imports, supply disruptions and higher global bond yields, which could add pressure to the balance of payments as the impact of foreign currency non-resident deposit inflows narrows.
"We stay cautious regarding the C/A and overall Balance of Payments outlook for FY27," the bank said, identifying oil prices, services export trends and seasonal gold demand as key factors to watch.
